problems: The new ChIP-seq evidence supports occupancy of the site by HNF4A, SOX13, and FOXP4 in HepG2, but does not establish allele-specific occupancy or which factor mediates a regulatory effect.
The QBiC-SELEX results are in-vitro binding predictions; they do not determine whether altered binding changes SORT1 transcription or in which direction.
SORT1 is strongly prioritized by the genetic and regulatory evidence, but no cited perturbation establishes that this element causally regulates SORT1.
The cited evidence supports cholesterol/LDL association, not an MI mechanism. The reported GWAS effect-allele labels alone do not establish the direction of the trait effect.

games.reason: HNF4A has stronger, closer HepG2 occupancy evidence at the variant (summit 15 bp away) and higher expression than SOX13, whose summit is 33 bp away (E25, E13; E26, E14). The HNF4A-mapped model predicts a clearer T-over-G binding increase (z 11.41; 7 family models pass), whereas the SOX13-mapped result predicts G-over-T binding but notes that family models disagree (z -8.25; 2 pass) (E13, E14). The T allele is also associated with increased SORT1 expression in liver (E09), directionally consistent with HNF4A’s predicted stronger binding on T, though the evidence does not establish TF-mediated transcription.

Both chains have evidence for HepG2 occupancy, but HNF4A is better supported: its ChIP-seq summit is closer to the variant (15 bp versus 33 bp for SOX13), and it has higher expression in the stated context. The HNF4A-family result predicts stronger binding on T, matching the T-associated increase in SORT1 expression; the SOX13-family models disagree on binding direction and predict stronger binding on G. This favors B, although neither chain establishes TF-mediated causality.
